intent: Extremely severe crashes
failure_type: Arbitrary fixed threshold used for defining extreme severity
expected_behavior: Identify crashes whose severity lies in the upper tail of the crash-severity distribution, using measures such as number of persons injured, number of persons killed, or combined severity indicators, rather than using a fixed constant like number_of_persons_injured > 10.

intent: Collisions with unusually high fatalities
failure_type: Arbitrary fixed thresholds used for defining unusually high fatalities and mixed severity signals
expected_behavior: Identify collisions whose fatality counts lie in the upper tail of the fatality distribution (e.g., extreme outliers), rather than using fixed constants like number_of_persons_killed >= 5 or mixing injury thresholds with fatality-based intent.

intent: Intersections with highest fatality rate
failure_type: Rate-based intent reduced to total count without normalization
expected_behavior: Compute fatality rate per intersection as total fatalities divided by number of collisions (or appropriate exposure), and rank intersections by this rate rather than by total fatalities.

intent: Areas where crash severity is worsening
failure_type: Temporal worsening reduced to aggregate severity ranking
expected_behavior: Identify areas where crash severity increases over time, such as rising injury/fatality severity across time windows, rather than ranking areas by total historical severity.

intent: Collisions requiring investigation
failure_type: Investigation criteria inferred without explicit policy definition
expected_behavior: Identify collisions that meet formally defined investigation criteria (e.g., fatalities, hit-and-run, specific contributing factors, or regulatory thresholds), rather than applying arbitrary or implicit rules.

intent: Find collisions involving commercial vehicles
failure_type: none
expected_behavior: Filter collisions involving commercial vehicles by matching vehicle type fields (e.g., vehicle_type_code_*), selecting rows where any vehicle corresponds to a commercial category.

intent: Vehicle types most frequently involved in crashes
failure_type: none
expected_behavior: Aggregate collisions by vehicle type (e.g., vehicle_type_code_1 through vehicle_type_code_5), count occurrences, and rank vehicle types by frequency to identify those most commonly involved in crashes.

intent: Areas where pedestrian injury risk is highest
failure_type: Risk-based intent reduced to count without normalization
expected_behavior: Compute pedestrian injury risk per area as a normalized measure (e.g., number of pedestrian injuries divided by number of collisions or probability of injury), and rank areas by this rate rather than raw counts.

intent: Collisions violating traffic law
failure_type: Traffic law violation inferred without explicit policy or legal mapping
expected_behavior: Identify collisions that meet defined traffic law violation criteria based on mapped contributing factors, violations, or legal classifications, rather than applying implicit or arbitrary interpretations.

intent: Increasing collision trend over time
failure_type: Temporal trend intent reduced to raw time-series listing without detecting increase
expected_behavior: Identify whether collision counts are increasing over time (e.g., rising trend across time windows such as months or years), rather than simply returning counts per date without analyzing the trend direction.

intent: Vehicles involved in extreme-impact collisions
failure_type: Arbitrary fixed thresholds used for defining extreme-impact collisions
expected_behavior: Identify collisions whose impact (e.g., fatalities, injuries, or combined severity) lies in the upper tail of the severity distribution, and then extract associated vehicle types, rather than using fixed constants like number_of_persons_killed >= 5 or number_of_persons_injured >= 40.

intent: Collisions exceeding reporting threshold
failure_type: Reporting threshold inferred without explicit policy definition
expected_behavior: Identify collisions that meet officially defined reporting thresholds (e.g., regulatory limits based on injuries, fatalities, property damage, or other criteria), rather than using arbitrary or assumed constants.

intent: Commercial vehicle crashes with multiple injuries
failure_type: none

intent: Find boroughs where total injuries exceed total fatalities
failure_type: none
expected_behavior: Aggregate collisions by borough, compute total injuries and total fatalities per borough, and return boroughs where total injuries exceed total fatalities.

intent: Vehicle types with increasing crash involvement
failure_type: Temporal increase intent reduced to static frequency aggregation
expected_behavior: Identify vehicle types whose crash involvement increases over time (e.g., rising counts across time windows such as months or years), rather than simply counting total crashes per vehicle type and sorting.

failure_type: none

intent: Intersections with unusually high nighttime crash activity
failure_type: none
expected_behavior: Identify intersections whose nighttime crash counts lie in the upper tail of the nighttime crash distribution.

intent: Time slots with unusually high crash frequency
failure_type: Fixed crash count threshold used to define high-frequency time slots instead of distribution-based detection
expected_behavior: Aggregate crash counts by crash_time hour-of-day, then identify hours in the upper tail of the hour-level crash-count distribution, rather than flagging any hour with more than N crashes.

intent: Vehicle types involved in unusually severe crashes
failure_type: Fixed injury count threshold applied to define severe crashes involving a vehicle type
expected_behavior: Compute average severity (persons injured + killed) per crash by vehicle type, then identify vehicle types where this severity measure is in the upper tail of the cross-vehicle-type distribution, not those exceeding a fixed injury threshold.

intent: ZIP codes with outlier crash densities
failure_type: Arbitrary fixed crash count used to define high-density ZIP codes
expected_behavior: Count crashes per zip_code and identify ZIP codes in the upper tail of the crash-count distribution across all ZIP codes, not ZIP codes exceeding a hardcoded threshold.

intent: Hours of day with unusually high pedestrian fatality risk
failure_type: Fixed fatality threshold or fixed hour window used instead of distribution-based detection
expected_behavior: Compute pedestrian fatality rate per hour (pedestrian killed / crashes in that hour) and identify hours in the upper tail of this rate distribution, not hours with fatalities exceeding a fixed count or falling in a manually specified time window.

intent: Streets with persistently recurring severe crashes across years
failure_type: Total crash count or severity count aggregated without checking for cross-year recurrence
expected_behavior: Identify streets (on_street_name) that appear in the upper severity tier in multiple distinct years — demonstrating structural danger, not just a one-time spike — rather than streets with the highest all-time aggregate crash count.

intent: Boroughs with accelerating cyclist injury rates
failure_type: Total cyclist injury count compared across two time points instead of computing a year-over-year growth rate
expected_behavior: Compute cyclist injury rate (cyclists injured per crash) per borough per year, then identify boroughs where this rate is consistently increasing across multiple consecutive years, not boroughs with the highest total cyclist injury count.

intent: Contributing factors with increasing crash prevalence over time
failure_type: Aggregate contributing factor frequency used without computing its share of crashes over time
expected_behavior: Compute the share of crashes attributed to each contributing factor per year, and identify factors where this share consistently increases across multiple years, not factors with the highest total occurrence count.

intent: Vehicle types with highest injury rate per crash involvement
failure_type: Total injury count used instead of injuries per crash involvement for the vehicle type
expected_behavior: Compute average total persons injured per crash for crashes involving each vehicle type, then rank vehicle types by this per-crash rate, not by the raw total injury count across all crashes involving that type.

intent: Contributing factors with highest lethality ratio
failure_type: Total fatality count used instead of fatalities-to-total-casualties ratio
expected_behavior: Compute the lethality ratio as number_of_persons_killed / (number_of_persons_killed + number_of_persons_injured) per contributing factor, then rank by this ratio. Factors in fewer but more lethal crashes would otherwise be obscured by high-frequency low-lethality ones.

intent: Time slots with highest pedestrian-to-motorist injury ratio
failure_type: Raw pedestrian injury count used instead of the pedestrian-to-motorist injury ratio
expected_behavior: Compute the ratio of total pedestrian injuries to total motorist injuries per hour of day, and rank hours by this ratio to identify when pedestrians bear a disproportionate share of injury risk relative to motorists.
semantic_requirements: ratio computation across two injury dimensions

intent: Distracted driving crashes
failure_type: Distracted driving inferred from loose keyword matching on contributing factor without legal definition
expected_behavior: There is no authoritative column for distracted driving classification. Inferring it via contributing_factor LIKE '%distract%' or '%phone%' applies a loose approximation without a formal legal mapping to the actual contributing factor values in the schema.

intent: Preventable crashes
failure_type: Preventability inferred from contributing factors using heuristic keyword matching without a formal preventability framework
expected_behavior: Preventability is a legal and policy concept not defined in the schema. Any SQL inferring preventability from contributing_factor string patterns (e.g., LIKE '%failure%', LIKE '%inattention%') applies an undefined classification not grounded in the data model.

intent: Crashes involving impaired driving
failure_type: Impaired driving inferred from keyword matching on contributing factor without legal BAC or intoxication definition
expected_behavior: Impaired driving is a legal concept requiring a blood-alcohol threshold or official classification. Inferring it via contributing_factor ILIKE '%alcohol%' OR '%drugs%' uses an informal approximation; the schema contains no authoritative impairment indicator.

intent: Minor accidents
failure_type: Minor accident threshold inferred from arbitrary injury count cutoff without legal or policy definition
expected_behavior: The schema has no column for accident classification. Defining a minor accident as number_of_persons_injured = 0 AND number_of_persons_killed = 0 is one interpretation but ignores property damage, which is a key legal criterion. Without a policy definition, this inference is ungrounded.

intent: Boroughs with worst pedestrian safety record
failure_type: Total pedestrian injury count used instead of pedestrian injury rate per crash or per population
expected_behavior: Pedestrian safety should be measured by pedestrian injuries per crash (or per unit of exposure), not total pedestrian injury count. Boroughs with more crashes would otherwise rank worst purely because of volume, masking genuine rate differences.

intent: Streets with most dangerous conditions
failure_type: Collision count used as proxy for danger rather than severity-weighted rate per street
expected_behavior: Street danger should reflect injury or fatality rate per crash on that street, not raw collision count. A busy intersection with many low-severity crashes is less dangerous than one with fewer but consistently severe crashes.

intent: Vehicle types most responsible for cyclist injuries
failure_type: Vehicle type ranked by total crash involvement count rather than cyclist injury rate per crash involvement
expected_behavior: Responsibility for cyclist injuries should be measured by the average number of cyclists injured per crash where the vehicle type appears, not the total number of crashes or total cyclist injuries — common vehicle types would otherwise dominate by volume.

intent: Total crashes per borough
failure_type: none
expected_behavior: COUNT(*) GROUP BY borough, ordered by count descending. Straightforward aggregation with no semantic ambiguity.

intent: Most common contributing factors in fatal crashes
failure_type: none
expected_behavior: Filter to crashes where number_of_persons_killed > 0, then count occurrences of contributing_factor_vehicle_1, order by count descending. Clear filter condition and aggregation with no distributional ambiguity.

intent: Crashes occurring between 7am and 9am
failure_type: none
expected_behavior: Filter crashes where EXTRACT(HOUR FROM crash_time) BETWEEN 7 AND 9. The time window is explicitly stated — no policy inference or distributional reasoning required.

intent: Average number of persons injured per crash by vehicle type
failure_type: none
expected_behavior: Compute AVG(number_of_persons_injured) per vehicle_type_code_1, ordered by average descending. Rate is explicitly requested and denominator is implied by GROUP BY — no distributional ambiguity.

intent: Total number of crashes per year
failure_type: none
expected_behavior: SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM crash_date) AS year, COUNT(*) FROM crashes GROUP BY year ORDER BY year. Simple temporal aggregation — no trend detection or distributional reasoning required.

intent: Crashes that resulted in at least one fatality
failure_type: none
expected_behavior: SELECT * FROM crashes WHERE number_of_persons_killed >= 1. Threshold is explicitly stated — no distributional reasoning needed.

intent: Total pedestrian injuries and fatalities by borough
failure_type: none
expected_behavior: SELECT borough, SUM(number_of_pedestrians_injured), SUM(number_of_pedestrians_killed) FROM crashes GROUP BY borough. Direct multi-column aggregation.

intent: Most common vehicle types involved in crashes
failure_type: none
expected_behavior: COUNT occurrences of vehicle_type_code_1 GROUP BY vehicle_type_code_1 ORDER BY count DESC. Straightforward frequency ranking with no rate or distributional inference.

intent: Crashes involving more than 3 persons injured
failure_type: none
expected_behavior: SELECT * FROM crashes WHERE number_of_persons_injured > 3. Threshold explicitly stated in intent.

intent: Number of crashes per day of the week
failure_type: none
expected_behavior: SELECT EXTRACT(DOW FROM crash_date) AS day_of_week, COUNT(*) FROM crashes GROUP BY day_of_week ORDER BY day_of_week. Direct temporal grouping — no distributional inference.

intent: Crashes at a specific intersection of Broadway and 42nd Street
failure_type: none
expected_behavior: Filter WHERE on_street_name ILIKE '%BROADWAY%' AND cross_street_name ILIKE '%42%'. Intersection is explicitly named — no policy inference.

intent: Average number of persons injured per crash by borough
failure_type: none
expected_behavior: SELECT borough, AVG(number_of_persons_injured) FROM crashes GROUP BY borough. Direct per-group average — rate is implicit in AVG and no normalization inference needed.

intent: Crashes where cyclists were involved
failure_type: none
expected_behavior: SELECT * FROM crashes WHERE number_of_cyclist_injured > 0 OR number_of_cyclist_killed > 0. Direct filter on explicit cyclist columns.

intent: Top 10 most frequent contributing factors across all crashes
failure_type: none
expected_behavior: COUNT occurrences of contributing_factor_vehicle_1, ORDER BY count DESC, LIMIT 10. Straightforward frequency ranking — no rate, threshold, or policy inference needed.
